text:
NOC-bot: 🚨 High error rate detected on serving-runtime-prefill cluster: 5xx spike, multiple container restarts detected. Rolling window 2m.
Priya: @Jamal you're oncall — can you confirm? I'm seeing alerts for OOM on a subset of GPU nodes.
Jamal: taking. joining console now. what's the impact?
Priya: ~15% of generation requests for a few customers returning 5xx or timing out, errors line up with container restarts for prefill service.
pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-4452 — Serving runtime prefill OOM spike. Pager: Jamal. Severity: P2 (investigating).
Jamal: ok, looking at logs from the affected pod pool (prefill-v2). pulling recent stack traces.
Anya: past 10m from pod prefill-v2-5c9f:
```
[2026-03-15T01:32:42Z] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 26.15 GiB already allocated; 2.92 GiB free; 28.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
Stack trace: /opt/runtime/infer/prefill_worker.py line 214
Restarting container: kubelet: Container cannot be started: prefill OOMKill
Pod prefill-v2-5c9f status: CrashLoopBackOff
```
Jamal: looks like OOM during prefill for very long prompts / huge context tokens. Any recent traffic changes or new model rolled out?
Priya: No model rollout. Noticed a handful of customers sending concatenated transcripts with 130k token contexts in last 30m. Prefill is trying to allocate KV cache for whole sequence.
Anya: corroborating — request sample (redacted):
```json
{"user_id":"acct_AAA","prompt_len_tokens":131482,"model":"redwood-7b-v2"}
```
Jamal: that's huge. Our prefill path doesn't stream-kv for that size; it tries allocate full KV on GPU and hits OOM. Need immediate mitigation to stop further restarts.
Rafael: proposed mitigations (fast to deploy):
- add request size guard at ingress to reject > 65k tokens with 413, with link to docs
- enable CPU-prefill fallback for over-threshold requests (dedicated path)
- scale out prefill pool temporarily and cordon noisy pods
Evan: customer-impact note: we can see 4 customer sessions with >100k tokens; 2 of them are production paying tenants (cust-XX, cust-YY) seeing 503s. CS notified.
Jamal: action plan: 1) put temporary nginx ingress rule to reject huge prefill payloads, 2) cordon prefill-v2 nodes that are flapping to avoid cascade, 3) enable CPU-prefill for oversized requests, 4) rolling restart of stable pods. I'm going to patch ingress.
Priya: I can push the ingress rule. Payload check regex ready, will return 413 + info header.
Anya: while Priya pushes, I'm collecting crashloop backoff pods list and snapshotting pv memory metrics.
Priya: applied ingress size guard (nginx):
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: prefill-ingress-sizeguard-temp
spec:
  rules:
  - http:
      paths:
      - path: /prefill
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: prefill-service
            port:
              number: 80
EOF
# nginx config map updated to reject body > 2MB (translates to ~65k tokens)
```
Anya: immediately seeing a drop in OOM events after the guard. Crashloop count down from 7->3 in last 2 minutes.
Jamal: good. Rafael can you toggle CPU-prefill path? That should accept oversized requests on CPU to avoid GPU OOMs (slower but better than crash).
Rafael: enabling CPU-prefill route now — flipping rollout traffic rule to 10% for oversized token path.
Evan: CS updated customers cust-XX and cust-YY: they saw intermittent 503s for 12m, we advised temp mitigation and asked them to reduce context or use chunked calls.
Anya: collecting kube describe on one flapping pod:
```
Name: prefill-v2-5c9f
Events:
  Normal  BackOff  30s (x5 over 5m)  kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container
  Warning  OOMKilled  29s (x5 over 5m)  kubelet  Container killed due to OOM
Logs excerpt: CUDA out of memory while allocating KV cache for sequence length 131482
```
Jamal: rolling restart of remaining stable prefill pods to clear GPU memory fragmentation. Priya to coordinate safe window.
Priya: restarting stable pods in batches of 2 to preserve capacity.
Rafael: also recommending a config change to the runtime: proactively reject or stream KV for requests > 65k tokens. Filing runtime PR now.
Anya: created runtime issue RN-1098: "prefill: prevent full-GPU KV allocation for >65k tokens; add streaming fallback" and linked to incident.
pagerduty-bot: Incident update PD-4452: mitigation in place (ingress guard + CPU-prefill fallback). Notifying stakeholders.
Evan: quick customer impact summary for postmortem: 2 paying customers impacted, ~20 failed requests, peak error rate 18% on prefill path for 12m. No data loss.
Jamal: handoff to Rafael for overnight watch after we verify stability for 30m. Rafael — please own followups and postmortem.
Rafael: taking handoff. I've got alert on my phone. Next steps: monitor OOMs for 2h, push runtime PR to add server-side guard, propose default reject at 65k tokens with explicit error message + docs.
Priya: confirming ingress guard + CPU-prefill active. Will keep scaling headroom and watch latency regressions (CPU-prefill adds ~700-1200ms).
Anya: attaching links to logs and pod snapshots in incident doc (private): <internal-link>/incidents/PD-4452/logs
Jamal: thanks team. reopening if regressions. closing this live mitigation.
Rafael: noted. assigning postmortem owner: Rafael. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.
NOC-bot: Alert quieted. Error rate back to baseline.
